\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.CSPTesterExamples}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Predicate for equations with at most three variables]
\lean{FABL.MaxThreeLinPredicate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p184-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002
}
\label{FABL.MaxThreeLinPredicate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
A predicate for a linear equation over the field with two elements is specified by an
index in $\{0,1,2,3\}$, giving the number of variables in the equation, and a right-hand
side in that field.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[At most three-variable linear predicate template]
\lean{FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p184-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b004
}
\label{FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CSPTemplate, FABL.MaxThreeLinPredicate, FABL.𝔽₂}
Over the two-element field $\mathbb{F}_2$- let's use $\mathbb{F}_2$, consider predicates given
by a linear equation in at most three variables, with right-hand side in $\mathbb{F}_2$.
The template evaluates an equation as satisfied exactly when the sum of the queried
field elements equals its right-hand side.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Arity of a linear predicate]
\lean{FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate_arity}
\label{FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate_arity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.MaxThreeLinPredicate, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
\difficulty{1}
For every maximum-at-most-three linear predicate, its arity in the associated constraint
template equals its arity index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Maximum arity of the linear template]
\lean{FABL.maxArity_maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
\label{FABL.maxArity_maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CSPTemplate.maxArity, FABL.MaxThreeLinPredicate, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
\difficulty{4}
The maximum arity of the maximum-at-most-three linear constraint template is $3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Three-term sum criterion in characteristic two]
\lean{FABL.f₂_add_add_eq_zero_iff_eq_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb F_2$, $a+b+c=0$ if and only if $c=a+b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Odd-weight partial-sum variable set]
\lean{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable}
\leanok
For each natural number $m$, the variable set is the disjoint union of $m+2$
input-coordinate indices and $m+1$ proof-coordinate indices.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Predicate for an odd-weight partial-sum check]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPPredicate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002
}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPPredicate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.MaxThreeLinPredicate, FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed}
For each natural number $m$, associate a linear predicate to a seed in the disjoint
union of a Boolean flag and $m$ indices: the flag $\mathrm{false}$ gives a
three-variable equation with right-hand side $0$; the flag $\mathrm{true}$ gives a
one-variable equation with right-hand side $1$; and any index seed gives a
three-variable equation with right-hand side $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial constraint coordinates]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFirstCSPScope}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFirstCSPScope}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable}
For each natural number $m$, the initial constraint selects, in order, the input
coordinates with indices $0$ and $1$, followed by the proof coordinate with index $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Final constraint coordinate]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFinalCSPScope}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFinalCSPScope}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable}
For each natural number $m$, the final constraint selects the single proof coordinate
with index $m$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Intermediate constraint coordinates]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumStepCSPScope}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumStepCSPScope}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable}
For each natural number $m$ and each index $k<m$, the constraint at step $k$ selects, in
order, the proof coordinate with index $k$, the input coordinate with index $k+2$, and
the proof coordinate with index $k+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Constraint coordinates for each seed]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPScope}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPScope}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed, FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPPredicate, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFinalCSPScope, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFirstCSPScope, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumStepCSPScope}
For each natural number $m$, the scope associated with a seed is the initial scope for
the flag $\mathrm{false}$, the final scope for the flag $\mathrm{true}$, and the
intermediate scope at index $k$ for an index seed $k<m$. Thus its ordered list of
coordinates has length three for the false-flag and index seeds, and length one for the
true-flag seed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Odd-weight partial-sum uniform tester]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumUniformStringTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumUniformStringTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed, FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable, FABL.UniformStringTester, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPPredicate, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPScope, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFirstCSPScope, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumStepCSPScope}
For each natural number $m$, choose uniformly from the finite seed set consisting of a
Boolean flag and $m$ indices. The false-flag and index seeds select three-variable
linear equations with right-hand side $0$, while the true-flag seed selects a
one-variable linear equation with right-hand side $1$; each seed queries its associated
ordered coordinates, and every variable in the disjoint union of $m+2$ input coordinates
and $m+1$ proof coordinates is queried for at least one seed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Odd-weight partial-sum assignment]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPAssignment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p186-b001
}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a Boolean sequence $w$ of length $m+2$ and a Boolean sequence $q$ of length $m+1$,
assign to each variable in the disjoint union of these two index sets the corresponding
value of $w$ or $q$, viewed as an element of the field with two elements.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Predicate Evaluation and Partial Sum Checks]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPPredicate_eval}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPPredicate_eval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckHolds, FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed, FABL.f₂_add_add_eq_zero_iff_eq_add, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPAssignment, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPPredicate, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumCSPScope, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFinalCSPScope, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumFirstCSPScope, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumStepCSPScope, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
\difficulty{4}
For every seed $s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\sqcup\mathrm{Fin}(m)$, input word
$w:\mathrm{Fin}(m+2)\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and proof word
$q:\mathrm{Fin}(m+1)\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, the linear predicate selected
by $s$, evaluated on the corresponding scoped variables assigned by $(w,q)$, returns
true exactly when the partial sum check specified by $s$ holds for $w$ and $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the odd weight variable set]
\lean{FABL.card_oddWeightPartialSumVariable}
\label{FABL.card_oddWeightPartialSumVariable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumVariable}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $m$, the disjoint union of a set with $m+2$ elements and a set
with $m+1$ elements has cardinality $2(m+2)-1$.
\end{theorem}

For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, Boolean input word $w$ of length $m+2$, and Boolean proof
word $q$ of length $m+1$, the uniform string tester's acceptance equals the value of its
associated constraint satisfaction instance under the assignment given by $w$ and $q$;
that value is the fraction of constraints satisfied, counted with their multiplicities.
\end{theorem}

For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, Boolean input word $w$ of length $m+2$, and Boolean proof
word $q$ of length $m+1$, the uniform string tester's acceptance is the expected value,
over a uniformly chosen seed
$s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\sqcup\mathrm{Fin}(m)$, of the indicator that the
partial-sum check specified by $s$ holds for $w$ and $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[BLR query triple]
\lean{FABL.blrQueryTriple}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002
}
\label{FABL.blrQueryTriple}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube}
For two functions $x,y$ from an $n$-element index set to the field with two elements,
their query triple is the function on three indices with values $x$, $y$, and $x+y$,
respectively.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BLR query collision condition]
\lean{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002}
\label{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube}
For two functions $x,y$ from an $n$-element index set to the field with two elements,
the collision condition holds precisely when $x$ is zero, $y$ is zero, or $x=y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Zero-query CSP scope]
\lean{FABL.blrZeroCSPScope}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002}
\label{FABL.blrZeroCSPScope}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube}
For each natural number $n$, the zero-query scope is the injection from a singleton
index set into the functions from an $n$-element index set to the field with two
elements that sends its sole index to the zero function.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Constant Value of the Zero Scope]
\lean{FABL.blrZeroCSPScope_apply}
\label{FABL.blrZeroCSPScope_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.blrZeroCSPScope}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $i$ be the unique element of a singleton index
set. The value of the zero scope at $i$ is the zero vector in $(\mathbb F_2)^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Distinct BLR query scope]
\lean{FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002}
\label{FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.blrQueryTriple}
Let $x$ and $y$ be functions from an $n$-element index set to the field with two
elements, and suppose neither is zero and they are unequal. The distinct-query scope is
the injection from a three-element index set that sends its indices, in order, to $x$,
$y$, and $x+y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[First Query in the Distinct Scope]
\lean{FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope_zero}
\label{FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $x,y\in(\mathbb F_2)^n$ be such that $x\ne0$,
$y\ne0$, and $x\ne y$. The first vector in the ordered scope $(x,y,x+y)$ is $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second Query in the Distinct Scope]
\lean{FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope_one}
\label{FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $x,y\in(\mathbb F_2)^n$ be such that $x\ne0$,
$y\ne0$, and $x\ne y$. The second vector in the ordered scope $(x,y,x+y)$ is $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Third Query in the Distinct Scope]
\lean{FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope_two}
\label{FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope_two}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $x,y\in(\mathbb F_2)^n$ be such that $x\ne0$,
$y\ne0$, and $x\ne y$. The third vector in the ordered scope $(x,y,x+y)$ is $x+y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[BLR CSP constraint]
\lean{FABL.blrCSPConstraint}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002
}
\label{FABL.blrCSPConstraint}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide, FABL.CSPConstraint, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope, FABL.blrZeroCSPScope, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
Let $x$ and $y$ be functions from an $n$-element index set to the field with two
elements. The associated constraint uses the linear equation whose right-hand side is
zero: if $x=0$, $y=0$, or $x=y$, it has arity one and scope consisting of the zero
function; otherwise it has arity three and scope $(x,y,x+y)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BLR CSP predicate]
\lean{FABL.blrCSPPredicate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002
}
\label{FABL.blrCSPPredicate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.MaxThreeLinPredicate, FABL.blrCSPConstraint}
Let $x$ and $y$ be functions from an $n$-element index set to the field with two
elements. The associated predicate is the predicate of their BLR constraint: it
specifies a linear equation with right-hand side zero, of arity one when $x=0$, $y=0$,
or $x=y$, and of arity three otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BLR CSP scope]
\lean{FABL.blrCSPScope}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002
}
\label{FABL.blrCSPScope}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.blrCSPConstraint, FABL.blrCSPPredicate, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
Let $x$ and $y$ be functions from an $n$-element index set to the field with two
elements. The scope of their BLR constraint is the ordered tuple of variables used by
that constraint: it consists of the zero function alone if $x=0$, $y=0$, or $x=y$, and
otherwise consists of $x$, $y$, and $x+y$, in that order.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Blr csp constraint eq zero of collision]
\lean{FABL.blrCSPConstraint_eq_zero_of_collision}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002}
\label{FABL.blrCSPConstraint_eq_zero_of_collision}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.blrCSPConstraint, FABL.blrZeroCSPScope}
\difficulty{1}
% dataset-pipeline: stub -- prose pending build_informal_statements.py
Statement pending regeneration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[BLR constraint in the distinct-query case]
\lean{FABL.blrCSPConstraint_eq_distinct_of_not_collision}
\label{FABL.blrCSPConstraint_eq_distinct_of_not_collision}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.blrCSPConstraint, FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $x,y$ be vectors in $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^n$.
If $x\neq 0$, $y\neq 0$, and $x\neq y$, then the constraint assigned to $(x,y)$ is the
linear equation with right-hand side $0$ on the three distinct variables $x$, $y$, and
$x+y$, in that order.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-addition in the field with two elements]
\lean{FABL.f₂_add_self}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
For every element $a$ of the field with two elements, $a+a=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-sum in the binary cube]
\lean{FABL.f₂Cube_add_self}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.f₂_add_self}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and every vector $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, $x+x=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[At most three-variable linear constraint evaluation]
\lean{FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinConstraintEval}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p186-b001
}
\label{FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinConstraintEval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CSPConstraint, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let a constraint apply a linear equation over the two-element field to an ordered tuple
of distinct variables, with arity at most three, and let an assignment give each
variable a value in that field. The constraint evaluation is true exactly when the sum
of the assigned values on its scope equals the equation’s right-hand side.
\end{definition}

\proofstep
  {FABL.f₂CoordinateVector_apply_self}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:(\mathbb F_2)^n\to\mathbb F_2$, and let
$x,y\in(\mathbb F_2)^n$. The predicate selected for the associated constraint, evaluated
on the values of $f$ at its scope, is true exactly when $f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)$ in $\mathbb
F_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate vector over the two-element field]
\lean{FABL.f₂CoordinateVector}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube}
For a positive integer $n$ and an index $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the $i$th coordinate
vector in $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^n$ has value $1$ at coordinate $i$ and value $0$ at
every other coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate vector at its index]
\lean{FABL.f₂CoordinateVector_apply_self}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂CoordinateVector}
\difficulty{1}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every index $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the $i$th
coordinate of the $i$th standard coordinate vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate vectors are nonzero]
\lean{FABL.f₂CoordinateVector_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂CoordinateVector}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every coordinate index $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the
corresponding standard coordinate vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct coordinate vectors]
\lean{FABL.f₂CoordinateVector_ne_of_ne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂CoordinateVector}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and distinct indices $i,j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the
corresponding standard coordinate vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ are distinct.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[BLR uniform string tester]
\lean{FABL.blrUniformStringTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p187-b002
}
\label{FABL.blrUniformStringTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BLRQueriesCollide, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.UniformStringTester, FABL.blrCSPConstraint, FABL.blrCSPConstraint_eq_distinct_of_not_collision, FABL.blrCSPConstraint_eq_zero_of_collision, FABL.blrCSPPredicate, FABL.blrCSPScope, FABL.blrDistinctCSPScope, FABL.blrZeroCSPScope, FABL.f₂CoordinateVector, FABL.f₂CoordinateVector_ne_of_ne, FABL.f₂CoordinateVector_ne_zero, FABL.maxAtMostThreeLinTemplate}
For each integer $n\ge 2$, there is a tester for strings in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ whose seed
is a uniformly chosen pair of strings in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The seed determines a BLR
constraint and its ordered query scope, and every coordinate of the string belongs to
the scope for at least one seed.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p185-b004}
Let $n$ be a natural number with $2\le n$, and let $f:(\mathbb F_2)^n\to\mathbb F_2$.
The acceptance probability of the uniform string tester for the BLR constraints equals
the value of the associated constraint satisfaction instance on the assignment $f$.
\end{theorem}
